cards.text: The Israelites set out and camp at Oboth, then at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab, then in the Valley of Zered. Pack up, set up, pack up AGAIN. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer without moving an inch, and these folks move three times in three verses.

cards.question: Next they camp on the far side of the Arnon. Numbers says the Arnon is the border between the Moabites and the ___.
To back up where that border runs, Numbers quotes an old book about the wadis of the Arnon. What's that book called?

answers.text: The Book of the Wars of the LORD
The Book of the Kings of Israel

cards.text: Next stop is Beer, the well, and that's where the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader. Friend, a well in the WILDERNESS is like finding a warm cookie at the bottom of a junk drawer.

cards.question: At Beer, the LORD tells Moses, "Gather the people so that I may give them ___."
True or false: at the well, Israel sings a song.
Israel's song at the well says who dug it. Who?

cards.text: The song starts, "Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!" and the nobles dig it out "with their scepters and with their staffs." SCEPTERS, friend, that's the CEO showing up in the good suit and grabbing a shovel.

From the wilderness they keep going: Mattanah, Nahaliel, Bamoth, and on to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland. If you're keeping a list, friend, put the pencil down and just know they're still moving.
Then Israel sends messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites. No sneaking around, friend. They knock on the front door first.

cards.question: What do Israel's messengers ask Sihon for?

answers.text: Permission to pass through his land
A share of the water in his wells
Soldiers to help them fight Moab

cards.question: True or false: Israel promises Sihon they'll stay on the King's Highway and won't even drink water from any well.
That's about as polite as a request gets. How does Sihon answer Israel?

answers.text: He gathers his whole army and attacks
He lets them pass for a fee
He sends them on a longer road

cards.text: Sihon fights Israel at Jahaz, and Israel puts him to the sword and takes his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok. Friend, they asked to walk down his hallway, and he lost the WHOLE HOUSE.

cards.question: Israel's new land stops at the border of the Ammonites. Why does the text say it stops there?

cards.text: Israel captures all the cities of the Amorites and moves right in, Heshbon and all its villages included.

cards.question: Heshbon was Sihon's city. Before Israel came, Sihon had fought the former king of ___ and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.

cards.text: That's why the poets sing, "Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored." Then the song turns toward Moab.

cards.question: In the poets' song, what goes out from Heshbon, the city of Sihon?

cards.text: It consumed Ar of Moab, and the song cries, "Woe to you, O Moab!" By the end, Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon.
So Israel settles into the land of the Amorites. Then Moses sends spies to a place called Jazer.

cards.question: True or false: after the spies go to Jazer, Israel makes peace with the Amorites living there.

cards.text: Then Israel turns up the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, comes out with his whole army to meet them in battle at Edrei. One king down, and the next one's already lining up.

cards.question: Og and his whole army are out there at Edrei. What's the first thing the LORD tells Moses about Og?
The LORD says He has delivered Og into Moses' hand, and tells Moses to do to Og what he did to ___.
True or false: at Edrei, Og's army survives the battle and escapes back into Bashan.

cards.text: Israel strikes down Og, his sons and his whole army, until no remnant is left, and they take possession of his land. The LORD said don't fear him, and friend, by the end there was nothing left TO fear.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "Gather the people so that I may give them ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of Israel's wilderness journey, but the opening card gives no context. It never says who the Israelites are following or where they are traveling, so the baker gets a list of camps with no frame.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Most of stop 1's choice cards are pure discovery questions with no setup to reason from. Card 2 (Amorites vs Edomites vs Ammonites), card 3 (the name of the quoted book) and card 7 (who dug the well) can only be guessed. That is 3 of the stop's 5 choice cards. Card 3 also asks about a detail the baker doesn't need to understand the passage.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Cards 6 and 7 already asked about the song (v17) and who dug the well (v18). Card 8 then steps back to retell v17-18. The story moves backward and repeats what was just asked instead of setting it up first.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says the poets sing. The text says the poets say (Numbers 21:27).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: One story card carries three beats: the fire consuming Ar of Moab, the woe to Moab, and Heshbon destroyed as far as Dibon.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card skips the poem's turn in v30, "But we have overthrown them." Without it, the baker misses the point of the poem: Sihon had taken Moab's land, and now Sihon has been overthrown. The card jumps straight to Heshbon being destroyed with no sense of what changed.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The punchline about there being nothing left TO fear is a quip about Og, his sons and his whole army being wiped out with no remnant left. That makes light of a total slaughter instead of looking at the moment with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.
